name: hipaa-breach
title: HIPAA breach notification and individual rights
summary: Apply the US HIPAA regulations to an incident or a request: whether it is a breach, who must be told and by when, requests for access, amendment and accounting, how long records are kept, and civil money penalties.
description: Each task says what happened at an unnamed health care provider, health plan or business associate: what information was exposed, who knew what and when, how many people in which States, or what a patient asked for. The AI reads ten parts of the HIPAA regulations in 45 CFR and gives the answer they decide: a date, a yes or no, a choice, a count or an amount. Every field of the answer is checked, and a task passes only when all of them are right.

families.name: What counts as a breach
families.what: Whether an incident is a breach of unsecured protected health information, or falls under one of the exclusions.

families.name: Notice to individuals
families.what: When a breach counts as discovered, the latest date for notifying individuals, and the form the notice takes.

families.name: Media and Secretary notices
families.what: When the media and the Secretary must be told, on the thresholds of 500 and the yearly submission.

families.name: Substitute notice
families.what: Which form of substitute notice is needed when contact details are missing or out of date.

families.name: Business associate notice
families.what: A business associate's notice to the covered entity, and whose discovery starts the clock, with or without an agency relationship.

families.name: Law enforcement delay
families.what: Whether a law enforcement request holds back a notification, and until when.

families.name: Right of access
families.what: The time limits for a request for access, its extension, the grounds of denial and what a fee may include.

families.name: Amendment and accounting
families.what: The time limits for amendment and accounting requests, the disclosures an accounting lists, and suspensions.

families.name: Record retention
families.what: How long each document must be kept, and the date through which it is kept.

families.name: Civil money penalties
families.what: The penalty tier for a violation, its adjusted amounts and the cap for each calendar year.
